import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 2

def design(feats):
    # Filter out derived features (they're less reliable)
    non_derived_mask = [t != 'derived' for t in feats.types]
    non_derived_ids = [fid for fid, mask in zip(feats.ids, non_derived_mask) if mask]
    
    # Compute effect sizes and p-values for each feature
    effects = []
    for fid in non_derived_ids:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        x = feats.x[:, col_idx]
        y = feats.y
        mean_y1 = np.mean(x[y == 1])
        mean_y0 = np.mean(x[y == 0])
        effect_size = mean_y1 - mean_y0
        
        # Welch's t-test
        group0 = x[y == 0]
        group1 = x[y == 1]
        if len(group0) > 1 and len(group1) > 1:
            t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(group0, group1, equal_var=False)
        else:
            p_val = 1.0
            
        effects.append((fid, effect_size, p_val))
    
    # Sort by absolute effect size (descending)
    effects.sort(key=lambda x: abs(x[1]), reverse=True)
    
    # Select top candidates
    candidates = [f for f, _, _ in effects[:10]]
    
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in candidates]])
    to_remove = set()
    for i in range(len(candidates)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(candidates)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) >= 0.6:
                to_remove.add(candidates[j])
    
    selected_features = [f for f in candidates if f not in to_remove]
    
    # Try different models with increasing complexity
    best_drivers = ()
    best_score = -np.inf
    
    # Try single driver
    for fid in selected_features[:5]:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        X = feats.x[:, col_idx].reshape(-1, 1)
        model = LogisticRegression(penalty='l1', solver='liblinear')
        model.fit(X, feats.y)
        score = model.score(X, feats.y)
        if score > best_score:
            best_score = score
            best_drivers = (fid,)
    
    # Try two drivers
    for i in range(min(3, len(selected_features))):
        for j in range(i+1, min(4, len(selected_features))):
            fid1, fid2 = selected_features[i], selected_features[j]
            col_idx1 = feats.column(fid1)
            col_idx2 = feats.column(fid2)
            X = feats.x[:, [col_idx1, col_idx2]]
            model = LogisticRegression(penalty='l1', solver='liblinear')
            model.fit(X, feats.y)
            score = model.score(X, feats.y)
            if score > best_score:
                best_score = score
                best_drivers = (fid1, fid2)
    
    # For final design, we'll include all selected features
    columns = selected_features[:10]  # up to 10 features
    products = []
    loadings = {}
    
    # Simple weighted sum for loadings
    for fid in columns:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        x = feats.x[:, col_idx]
        # Weight by effect size (sign matters)
        effect_size = effects[[f for f, _, _ in effects].index(fid)][1]
        loadings[fid] = effect_size
    
    return Design(
        drivers=best_drivers,
        columns=tuple(columns),
        products=tuple(products),
        loadings=loadings
    )
